name: FeynmanModel
summary: Represents a model specified by off-shell Feynman rules.

syntaxes.description: stores the four model tables used by the Feynman backend.

details: ReadModel automatically returns this head when the selected model contains CalcHEP lgrngN.mdl rules instead of constructive ampsN.mdl amplitudes.
The four parts are the particle table, vertex table, independent parameters and dependent functions. ModelParameter keeps each model's parameters local, so several models can be used together.
Use the same CreateDiagrams and diagramAmplitudes workflow as for a constructive model. The model head selects ordered Dirac and Lorentz tensors with off-shell internal propagators.

The supported tree backend uses unitary gauge for massive vectors, excludes ghosts and Goldstones consistently, and retains the CalcHEP tensor auxiliary for the four-gluon interaction. Unsupported Majorana flow or higher-spin fields return Failure.
A Feynman vertex table is not a table of complete lower-point amplitudes. Use a constructive model containing complete amplitudes as the factorization model.

examples.description: Read the bundled massive-electron QED Feynman model.
Inspect the four tables without changing the model.

name: DiracWord
summary: Represents an ordered product of Dirac matrices and slashed momenta.

syntaxes.description: represents an ordered product of Dirac matrices and slashed momenta.

details: Arguments are operators in their written order. DiracWord is not a commutative Times product; exchanging two gamma matrices requires the corresponding Clifford identity.
DiracGamma, DiracGamma5 and DiracSlash are the supported operator types. An empty word represents the identity between fermion endpoints.
These objects are normally generated from a Feynman model. Use FeynmanToSpinorProducts after Lorentz indices have been contracted.

name: DiracGamma
summary: Represents a Dirac gamma matrix carrying a Lorentz index.

syntaxes.description: represents a Dirac gamma matrix carrying a Lorentz index.

details: Place gamma matrices inside DiracWord to retain their noncommutative order.
A conversion expression must contract every Lorentz index exactly twice. A free Lorentz index is an explicit unsupported input, rather than silently discarded.
The matrix conventions used by conversion are those of HEPCAT; do not import an overall sign from a different spinor convention.

name: DiracGamma5
summary: Represents the chirality matrix in an ordered Dirac word.

syntaxes.description: represents the chirality matrix in an ordered Dirac word.

details: DiracGamma5 is a symbol, not a function of a Lorentz index.
FeynmanToSpinorProducts uses gamma5 = diag(-1,+1) in its Weyl-block convention.
The position inside DiracWord matters. Chiral projectors are scalar combinations of the identity and this matrix.

name: DiracSlash
summary: Represents a momentum contracted with a Dirac gamma matrix.

syntaxes.description: represents a momentum contracted with a Dirac gamma matrix.

details: Use DiracSlash inside DiracWord, rather than multiplying it as an unordered matrix factor.
The momentum may be a composite or signed sum. Conversion retains internal momenta off shell.
Ordinary external Dirac identities may simplify a contracted bilinear, but no internal mass shell is inferred from a propagator.

name: LorentzIndex
summary: Labels a Lorentz slot in a Feynman tensor.

syntaxes.description: labels a Lorentz slot in a Feynman tensor.

details: LorentzIndex[slot, 2] denotes a second Lorentz slot for a tensor auxiliary.
Vertex-local slots are attached to the incident lines by diagram generation. They are not external particle numbers until the vertex has been attached.
A summed index must appear exactly twice in the expression passed to conversion.

name: LorentzMetric
summary: Represents the Minkowski metric with two Lorentz indices.

syntaxes.description: represents the Minkowski metric with two Lorentz indices.

details: It is a symbolic tensor used by the Feynman backend, with the HEPCAT (+,-,-,-) momentum convention.
FeynmanToSpinorProducts contracts metrics with the other tensors before producing spinor chains. It does not apply metric-component substitutions to spinor expressions by itself.

name: LorentzMomentum
summary: Represents a four-momentum carrying a Lorentz index.

syntaxes.description: represents a four-momentum carrying a Lorentz index.

details: The first argument is a Mom object or a supported momentum combination. The second is the Lorentz index contracted with another tensor.
It retains off-shell Feynman momentum information until the contraction/conversion stage.
This head is distinct from MomProd, which is a scalar product in the spinor representation.

name: LorentzScalarProduct
summary: Retains an off-shell scalar product in a Feynman rule.

syntaxes.description: retains an off-shell scalar product in a Feynman rule.

details: A CalcHEP momentum dot product is retained as this typed object before vertex momentum slots have been attached.
It does not apply p squared = mass squared to an internal momentum. The Feynman result must retain the full off-shell numerator.
After conversion, ordinary spinor expressions use MomProd or explicit momentum chains instead.

name: FermionBar
summary: Represents the left antifermion endpoint of an ordered Dirac chain.

syntaxes.description: represents the left antifermion endpoint of an ordered Dirac chain.

details: The endpoint uses an all-incoming external-leg label and its external mass.
The normal Dirac tag is "Dirac". Chiral fields use their model tags, rather than an assumed helicity label for a massive particle.
HEPCAT conversion uses bar v = (<p|,-[p|). This convention fixes relative signs in the Weyl blocks.

name: FermionKet
summary: Represents the right fermion endpoint of an ordered Dirac chain.

syntaxes.description: represents the right fermion endpoint of an ordered Dirac chain.

details: The endpoint uses an all-incoming external-leg label and its external mass.
The normal Dirac tag is "Dirac". Massive spin states are retained as spinor indices, not fixed by a chirality string.
HEPCAT conversion uses u = (-|p>,|p]). Massless Dirac external fields need an explicit helicity assignment for conversion.

name: DiracChain
summary: Represents an ordered external-fermion bilinear.

syntaxes.description: joins FermionBar and FermionKet endpoints through one DiracWord.

details: Order is part of the expression. Keep gamma matrices and internal momentum slashes inside the DiracWord.
All external labels follow HEPCAT's incoming convention. Internal Feynman numerator momenta remain off shell.
When several fermion lines occur, retain the explicit pairing and signs generated by diagramAmplitudes instead of rearranging endpoints by hand.

examples.input: bilinear = DiracChain[FermionBar[1, m, "Dirac"], DiracWord[], FermionKet[2, m, "Dirac"]]

examples.description: Convert its endpoints into spinor products.

name: PolarizationVector
summary: Represents an external vector wavefunction in the Feynman backend.

syntaxes.description: represents an external vector wavefunction in the Feynman backend.

details: The leg labels the external momentum, index is its Lorentz slot, and mass distinguishes massive from massless wavefunctions.
For a photon, helicity +1 or -1 selects its wavefunction. The corresponding process names use A.+ or A.-.
A massive vector retains two symmetric VectorSpinIndex labels during conversion. Distinct Feynman diagrams must use a common reference choice for a given external gauge particle.

name: VectorSpinIndex
summary: Labels one of the two symmetric little-group slots of a massive vector.

syntaxes.description: labels one of the two symmetric little-group slots of a massive vector.

details: The slot is 1 or 2. The pair belongs to a single spin-one external state, not to two distinct particles.
FeynmanToSpinorProducts keeps these explicit slots to preserve the vector spin tensor.
The SPINAS exporter combines the symmetric spinor components for one vector polarization before taking its squared modulus. Different external spin states are then summed incoherently.

name: ColorIndex
summary: Labels an external color state.

syntaxes.description: labels an external color state.

details: External color labels survive symbolic Feynman conversion. Internal color labels are local dummy indices.
An unresolved external color tensor is not a numerical color sum. The current complete SPINAS exporter refuses color-stripped families when a full color sum is required.

name: ColorDelta
summary: Represents a contracted color Kronecker tensor.

syntaxes.description: represents a contracted color Kronecker tensor.

details: The tensor is retained symbolically by the Feynman backend. It does not imply a sum over all external colors.
Keep the color contraction conventions of the supplied model when comparing with an independent numerical process.

name: ColorGenerator
summary: Represents a fundamental SU(3) generator.

syntaxes.description: represents a fundamental SU(3) generator.

details: The normalization follows CalcHEP's lambda/2 convention.
Argument order distinguishes the antifundamental, fundamental and adjoint slots. Reordering these slots can change the amplitude.
The backend retains color tensors; it does not infer missing external color sums or averages.

name: ColorStructure
summary: Represents an SU(3) structure constant.

syntaxes.description: represents an SU(3) structure constant.

details: This is the antisymmetric tensor f(a,b,c) in the imported CalcHEP convention.
The vertex's factor of i is retained separately. Do not add another i merely because this head denotes a structure constant.
Unresolved color tensors remain explicit through Feynman-to-spinor conversion.

name: FeynmanToSpinorProducts
summary: Converts contracted Feynman amplitudes to spinor products without imposing internal mass shells.

syntaxes.description: converts a contracted Feynman tensor expression.
preserves the external mass-rule pair.
converts a list of amplitude pairs.

details: The external convention is u = (-|p>,|p]), bar v = (<p|,-[p|), gamma5 = diag(-1,+1). All momenta remain incoming in the symbolic result.
Lorentz indices must be fully contracted. Unsupported tensors, free indices and unsupported fields return Failure rather than a partially converted amplitude.
Internal Feynman slashes and propagators remain off shell. Conversion applies ordinary algebra and external wavefunction conventions only.
Use the string option "FermionHelicities" for massless Dirac external fields. "ReferenceSpinors" supplies per-leg references; Automatic retains independent generic Xi references.
Raw diagrams can also be passed directly to PrepareAmplitudes with their FeynmanModel. That route performs conversion before reference selection and reduction.
For gauge invariance, use one reference assignment per external gauge leg for the entire Feynman sum, rather than optimizing separate Feynman diagrams independently.

name: WriteSPINASProcess
summary: Writes a complete, readable C++ process using SPINAS, with optional CalcHEP and helicity-resolved MadGraph validation.

syntaxes.description: exports one all-incoming amplitude at its fixed massless helicities.
combines helicity-related {particles, amplitude} entries into one class.
declares the physical process and crosses its outgoing legs automatically.

details: Inputs are symbolic all-incoming amplitudes. In the physical-process form, the concatenated incoming and outgoing lists fix the external-leg order, while each amplitude entry retains its all-incoming particle list. Do not pre-cross these formulas.
For example, a physical e,A -> e,A process has all-incoming species e,A,E,A. Outgoing momenta and angle-spinor signs are crossed exactly once by the exporter.

A generic massless name such as A requests its complete helicity sum. A.+, A.- or the string option "FixedHelicities" selects a specified helicity. Incomplete requested coverage is refused; missing amplitudes are not invented using parity.

Generated amp returns the complex amplitude for one external spin/helicity assignment. spin_sum adds |amp| squared over the requested states. Family amp2 also averages unfixed incoming states and applies the final identical-species factor once, including identical fermions.
The older fixed-helicity overload preserves its existing normalization convention. Use the physical-process or family form for a complete unpolarized process.

The default export writes source only. "Build" -> True compiles and links the existing SPINAS library; "RunExamples" -> True also runs three conserved physical example points. No external library is installed or rebuilt.

"SPINASDirectory" and "CMakeExecutable" support automatic build-tool discovery. Independent validation instead requires an explicit reference-generator directory and model selection. The SPINAS precision must match the library ABI. "Overwrite" -> True explicitly permits replacing an existing exported project.

The independent CalcHEP validator generates a reference process and compares common random points. Specify "CalcHEPDirectory" and "CalcHEPModel" -> {directory, modelNumber}; both default to None. "CalcHEPAllowedParticles" -> All retains the full chosen theory, while an explicit list of positive absolute PDGs restricts the reference particle sector. "RunCalcHEPValidation" -> True builds and runs it. The actual time-based seed is reported, and an explicit "CalcHEPSeed" or --seed value replays it.

A separate n_calchep target uses the SPINAS matrix element with CalcHEP's numerical phase-space integration, cuts, histograms and VEGAS. This bypasses symbolic CalcHEP generation and does not require an equivalent CalcHEPModel.

Numerical model constraints, masses and widths are connected to the numerical menus. Explicit amplitude width conventions remain authoritative. Unsupported automatic-width or gauge-restoring operations are refused.
Current complete numerical exports are colorless. Unresolved Xi spinors, hats, unsupported symbolic functions or color tensors must be resolved before exporting.

The independent MadGraph validator generates one unpolarized reference process and compares each exported massless-helicity combination separately. "RunMadGraphValidation" -> True builds and runs the check; "MadGraphPoints" -> 1000 and "MadGraphSeed" -> Automatic are the normal defaults. Massive external spins are summed because the two libraries may use different spin bases.

Specify "MadGraphDirectory" and "MadGraphModel" explicitly to select the independent reference generator and UFO theory; both default to None. "MadGraphAllowedParticles" -> All retains the full chosen model, or a list such as {11, 22} explicitly selects the electron/positron/photon sector. "MadGraphParameterRules" supplies external UFO input values when numerical matching needs an override. No theory or particle restriction is inferred from the HEPCAT process.

Generated projects contain validate_madgraph(options) and a process_validate_madgraph executable. ValidateMadGraph provides the corresponding Mathematica entry point, including a simple per-helicity table and optional detailed numerical diagnostics. MadGraph is not required for ordinary SPINAS evaluation.
"MadGraphParameterMap" maps HEPCAT parameter names to differently named UFO parameters. Used couplings and masses are checked rather than assumed from the external particle names.

MadGraph propagator widths are matched to the amplitude prescription. For bare HEPCAT PropDen denominators, unmatched adjustable reference widths are zeroed; explicit reference width rules and matched width parameters are preserved. Detailed validation reports record this choice.
The return value is the output directory. "ReturnDetails" -> True adds generated file paths, build information, normalization metadata and optional validation results.

When both independent reference checks are requested, both are attempted even if one fails. A requested numerical FAIL, unavailable reference or runtime error returns Failure; its ExportResult contains the generated project and both reference reports. Writing source or finishing compilation is not reported as a physics-validation success.

name: ValidateMadGraph
summary: Compares exported HEPCAT/SPINAS amplitudes with independent MadGraph matrix elements on common random phase-space points, separately for each massless-helicity combination.

syntaxes.description: builds and runs the MadGraph validator of a SPINAS project exported by the current WriteSPINASProcess.
exports and validates the supplied all-incoming amplitude entries for the declared physical process.
validates one all-incoming amplitude at its specified massless helicities, with IncomingLegs selecting the physical incoming pair.
returns the full report, including per-helicity failures and the actual random seed.

details: The default result is a compact table with one row for each exported massless-helicity combination. "Output" -> "Summary" gives status counts; "Output" -> "Details" retains the full diagnostic association.

The benchmark is calculated from MadGraph's own generated amplitudes, independently of the supplied HEPCAT expression. Both evaluations receive the same physical momenta and matched masses and couplings. This tests the expression and numerical export together.

Amplitude entries retain HEPCAT's all-incoming convention. Declare incoming -> outgoing as in WriteSPINASProcess; the exporter crosses outgoing momenta and angle spinors once. Do not cross the formulas manually before passing them.

The particles, amplitude, model overload mirrors the original fixed-helicity WriteSPINASProcess form and retains its normalization convention. Use the grouped physical-process form when validating a complete helicity family.

The reference process is generated without restricting its external helicities. The validator selects individual helicity vectors from that process, fixes the requested massless helicities and sums the massive-particle spin states. It therefore avoids assuming that the MadGraph and SPINAS massive spin bases are identical.

The default table displays massless helicities as leg:sign labels, such as 3:-, 4:+. A process with no massless helicities is labeled accordingly. Details retains the original exported leg-order vectors with doubled helicities: photons have entries +2 or -2, and zero entries do not select a massless helicity on that leg. Massive spin states are summed.

The comparison uses squared amplitudes. Complex amplitudes themselves may differ by external-state phase conventions. Initial spin averages and final identical-particle factors are applied consistently once, including cases where an incoming or outgoing massless helicity is fixed. Multiplying either amplitude by an overall phase, including -1 or I, is not a mismatch.

"MadGraphPoints" -> 1000 checks 1000 common physical points for each massless-helicity combination. "MadGraphSeed" -> Automatic chooses a time-based seed at runtime and records it. An explicit unsigned 64-bit integer, including zero, permits replay.

"RelativeTolerance" -> 10^-7 and "AbsoluteTolerance" -> 0 are the default comparisons. An absolute floor is not used to hide a wrong small amplitude. Nonfinite values, incomplete checks and evaluation errors cannot be reported as PASS. A failed report retains the first failing point and its momenta.

"MinimumEnergy" and "MaximumEnergy" bound the sampled center-of-mass energy; Automatic chooses values above the process thresholds. These are validation samples, not a phase-space integral or an analytic proof.

Choose "MadGraphDirectory" and "MadGraphModel" explicitly; neither an installation nor a theory is selected by default. The model is a UFO name or directory. For example, "sm-full" includes massive electrons and all Standard Model interactions. "MadGraphAllowedParticles" -> {11, 22} explicitly restricts that reference to the electron, positron and photon sector, excluding Z and Higgs exchange in pure-QED four-fermion tests. All, the default filter, retains the complete selected theory. Automatic model selection does not infer a theory.

Particle filters use positive absolute PDG codes and include the corresponding antiparticles. The list must contain every external particle type. A filter that omits an external state or names particles unavailable in the selected model cannot produce a passing comparison.

An explicitly supplied Automatic generator directory may consult the corresponding environment variables. It does not scan hard-coded installation directories. Passing the installation path directly makes the reference setup visible in the calculation.

Masses and used model parameters are matched to the supplied model. "MadGraphParameterRules" -> {"name" -> value, ...} overrides named external UFO inputs when needed. For a custom theory, ensure that its independent inputs and derived couplings agree with the HEPCAT model; ambiguous or inconsistent matching produces a diagnostic instead of a false pass.

"MadGraphParameterMap" -> {"HEPCATName" -> "UFOName", ...} identifies differently named model parameters. A mapping may target an external input or a derived UFO parameter whose value is checked. It does not replace the independent numeric inputs supplied by MadGraphParameterRules.

Propagator widths must use the same prescription on both sides. Bare HEPCAT PropDen denominators have no decay width, so unmatched, independently adjustable MadGraph decay-width inputs are set to zero. Explicit MadGraphParameterRules and width parameters used by the HEPCAT amplitude retain their supplied values. The detailed Reference report records the width policy and the zeroed or preserved inputs; an unsupported dependent-width mapping is reported before a comparison can pass.
"TimeConstraint" -> 600 bounds MadGraph reference preparation. It is not a deadline for the complete export, CMake build and numerical sampling operation.

The current numerical validator supports colorless tree-level processes with two incoming particles, at least two outgoing particles and external spins through one. It requires MadGraph, a Fortran compiler, SPINAS and the normal C++ build tools. Missing installations or unsupported inputs are reported explicitly; ordinary source-only SPINAS exports remain usable.

Validation can expose numerical conditioning as well as incorrect formulas. Expressions involving nearly cancelling terms or inverse small masses may lose precision at high energy even when an equivalent compact form is stable. Inspect detailed failures before changing tolerances.
The directory overload expects a project containing the MadGraph support emitted by the current WriteSPINASProcess. Regenerate an older project with that exporter before using this overload.

An exported project retains its process, model parameters, reference configuration and fixed-helicity selection. The directory overload changes sampling controls such as points, seed, tolerances, energy bounds and the reference preparation budget. To change a stored export setting, regenerate the project or use the amplitude-and-model overload; those overrides are rejected rather than silently ignored.
